steps.what: Observe aides' care and clarify patient needs and delegated responsibilities
Guide nurses' aides or assistants and address or escalate care concerns

tasks.design: Keep direct supervision and guidance with the nurse within verified local delegation rules. The {OTHER} clinical record can supply the care plan, but task completion flags do not replace observing practice.
tasks.previous_blocker: The nurse must understand actual practice and changing patient needs.
tasks.enabler_now: Record access can support supervision without doing it.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe care and giving timely, useful guidance.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a gap between a recorded completion and the patient's actual condition.
tasks.altitude: Supervision and escalation authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Local scope, supervision responsibilities and escalation criteria

evidence.claim: Direct supervision of care includes observation and guidance that a completion record does not replace.

assumptions: Boundary is this nurse's direct supervision, not assistants' care delivery or roster preparation. Local scope must be verified; the occupation title grants no additional authority.

Responsible clinicians produce the existing care plan outside this boundary with unchanged effort. The nurse elicits questions and produces supervision findings in s1, retaining all observation and capture time; missing context is clarified directly.
No structured competence score or risk feed is assumed. Review native care-plan access before any future custom tool; none is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because no changed software or process is proposed.
unknowns: Local delegation responsibilities and actual supervisory remit
research_questions: Which supervision failures arise from unclear delegation rather than missing software?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Routine guidance and unsafe-care concerns retain direct supervision time; no assumed dashboard saving.

tasks.short: Evaluate nursing intervention outcomes and confer with the team

steps.what: Assess nursing intervention outcomes against intended goals and patient response
Confer with healthcare team members on outcomes and required follow-up

tasks.design: Retain direct outcome assessment and team discussion using the {OTHER} clinical record as context. A displayed trend may support evaluation, but it does not determine whether an intervention helped this patient.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes may reflect several interventions or the underlying condition.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records can show observations without establishing causation.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting uncertain response and deciding when to escalate.
tasks.human_edge: Connect patient experience and observations and challenge an unsupported conclusion.
tasks.altitude: Outcome interpretation and clinical escalation remain within the existing professional remit.

reach.learn: Goal-linked observations and distinguishing association from treatment effect

evidence.claim: Interpreting an individual patient's nursing outcomes requires contextual assessment and professional discussion.

assumptions: Boundary covers assessment and team consultation, not treatment modification or a separately measured progress note.

Care staff produce dated intervention and observation entries during existing care outside this boundary, unchanged. The nurse checks them against current patient response in s1; missing information requires direct clarification in retained work.
No structured outcome classification or free patient assessment is presumed. Native record views are checked before any custom addition; none is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the design keeps the process unchanged. Any shared team-review encounter is allocated once.
unknowns: Outcome measures in use and available clinical supervision
research_questions: Which missing observations prevent a defensible evaluation in current practice?

already_counted.description: Patient outcome assessment and team discussion remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Clear improvement and uncertain outcomes both retain assessment and necessary consultation.

tasks.short: Assess needs, plan care and implement interventions as a team member

steps.what: Assess patient needs and contribute to care planning with the team
Implement agreed nursing interventions and respond to changes in patient needs

tasks.design: Keep team assessment, care planning and physical interventions with qualified staff using the {OTHER} clinical record. This design changes neither clinical decisions nor care delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task combines contextual decisions, coordination and direct patient care.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared records can support continuity without replacing bedside work.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting to changing needs while staying within delegated authority.
tasks.human_edge: Notice deterioration, communicate promptly and deliver appropriate care.
tasks.altitude: No change in care authority, team accountability or bedside time.

reach.learn: Local delegation, escalation and continuity requirements

evidence.claim: Team nursing assessment and physical intervention remain substantive human work.

assumptions: Boundary covers the focal nurse's team contribution and interventions, not colleagues' time. Local licensing and delegation determine actual scope.

The nurse elicits and reconciles observations and preferences in s1, including capture and plan entry. Team members supply findings through existing care work outside this baseline, unchanged; missing or conflicting instructions require direct clarification before intervention.
No complete structured needs assessment is assumed upstream. Native clinical-record functions are reviewed before future custom tools; none is added.
Zero incremental upkeep because the work remains unchanged. This broad task overlaps narrower outcome and care tasks, so roll-ups must allocate the same real action once.
unknowns: Local scope, care setting and division of team duties
research_questions: Which distinct clerical step can be measured without counting direct patient care as removable time?

tasks.short: Record patients' food and fluid intake and output

steps.what: Observe or measure patient food and fluid intake and output
Record food and fluid intake and output on the patient chart

tasks.design: Configure the native intake/output chart in the {OTHER} clinical record for point-of-care entry, with unit checks and visible incomplete measurements. The nurse still observes, measures, enters and checks each item; savings come from removing duplicate paper-to-record copying and manual chart totals where those exist.
tasks.previous_blocker: A paper bedside chart can require later copying and repeated totalling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native structured chart entry can hold the measured event once and calculate display totals.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing what was actually consumed or lost and identifying unreliable measurements.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise uncertainty and clarify a suspicious entry rather than presenting an invented precise value.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate chart work; observation and clinical interpretation remain with staff.

reach.task: Review a fluid chart for missing or inconsistent entries
reach.learn: Units, event timing and measurement limitations

evidence.claim: Direct structured chart entry can avoid duplicate transcription and calculate totals, while measurement and verification remain human work.

assumptions: Boundary is observation and recording of intake/output, not feeding, toileting assistance, prescribing fluid or interpreting balance clinically. The paper-and-recopy baseline is an E1 scenario to verify.

The nurse produces measured quantity, unit, intake/output category and uncertainty in s1. Patient identifier, event time, category, amount or food portion and recorder are captured and checked in retained s2 time; this is not a free structured input feed.

Unmeasured consumption stays unknown or explicitly estimated under local charting rules; no model turns food descriptions into invented volumes. Offline or incomplete entries use the existing paper/manual route and are reconciled with duplicate checks.
Test the native clinical-record chart and bedside device access before custom development. If direct entry and totals already exist, no duplicate-work saving is available.
Configuration does not add automated treatment decisions. Native runtime is not labour; only actual nurse copying and totalling can be saved.
unknowns: Whether duplicate entry exists, bedside access and true measurement versus recording time
research_questions: Does direct native entry halve chart work after counting measurement, field capture, uncertainty and offline reconciliation?

already_counted.description: Observation and measurement remain fully counted.
Point-of-care field capture, checking and manual fallback remain.

incremental.description: Nurse checks chart completeness, duplicate events and changed entry rules.
Clinical record owner maintains chart configuration and access.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=77.5, gross=22.5 less three focal upkeep hours gives net=19.5. High assumes duplicated chart work halves; low assumes current native entry or offline reconciliation leaves only upkeep-equivalent gain. Measurement time remains 55.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Direct care, supervision and clinical outcome discussion stay human; a verified duplicate-charting burden may be reduced through native entry.
reach: Improve delegation and care handovers with registered nurses
